• The Keeper of Halden Point

  For thirty-one years, Ada Marsh climbed the one hundred and twelve iron steps of the Halden Point lighthouse every evening at dusk. She carried a tin of
  paraffin, a rag, and a thermos of tea gone lukewarm in her coat pocket. Her hands knew the work better than her head did. Trim the wick. Check the lens. Turn
  the clockwork that spun the great glass prisms. Light the lamp before the fog came in from the sea.

  The station had been automated the year before her husband died, and the mainland office had sent a letter thanking her for her
